findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates an extra empty page when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit; use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — The public group-members page is limited to 50 members without pagination controls, making remaining members inaccessible through the public UI.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — Removing the PATCH-specific handler causes membership PATCH requests containing changes.add or changes.delete to return success without changing membership.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — Membership PATCH requests routed to the ordinary update action set visible to false because the visible parameter is absent.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — The public group-members page is limited to 50 members without pagination controls, making remaining members inaccessible through the public UI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the public group members route (group-members.js.es6) calls model.findMembers() which uses a limit of 50 (line 10 in group.js). Looking at the public group/members.hbs template, it only iterates over 'members' without any pagination controls (unlike the admin template which has next/previous actions). The admin controller has pagination actions (next, previous) but the public GroupMembersRoute does not have equivalent actions. This means public users can only see the first 50 members with no way to access the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — Removing the PATCH-specific handler causes membership PATCH requests containing changes.add or changes.delete to return success without changing membership.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that removing the PATCH-specific handler causes PATCH requests to return success without changing membership. However, looking at the diff, the old code had a conditional `if request.patch?` that called `update_patch(group)` which handled `params[:changes]` with add/delete arrays. The new code removes this entirely - there is no PATCH route handling at all in the new code. The routes.rb diff shows the new routes are `delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'` and `put 'members' => 'groups#add_members'` - completely different endpoints. The old PATCH functionality is intentionally replaced with new PUT/DELETE member endpoints, not broken. This is a deliberate API change, not a bug where PATCH requests silently succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — Membership PATCH requests routed to the ordinary update action set visible to false because the visible parameter is absent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the PATCH route handling was removed. The old code had `if request.patch?` calling `update_patch(group)`, but this entire conditional is removed in the new code. The new `update` method only handles PUT requests. There is no longer a PATCH route being handled by the update action - the routes.rb changes show PATCH is not configured for groups. The finding references behavior that no longer exists in the new code.
